headline: Ishraque Hossain resigns as state minister after gun display controversy
summary: The MP for Dhaka-6 announced his resignation at a press conference, stating he stepped down to avoid embarrassing the party and the Prime Minister.
details: Ishraque Hossain, the State Minister for Liberation War and Affairs, has resigned from his post. He formally announced the decision during a press conference at the National Press Club on Monday afternoon.
The resignation follows a controversy surrounding an anti-drug operation in the Gendaria area of the capital, where Ishraque was seen displaying his weapon in photos and videos.
Ishraque stated that he held the weapon for his own security during the operation, but claimed that the images were used by media and social media to overshadow the actual anti-drug efforts.
He explained that he stepped down to ensure that neither the Prime Minister nor his party would be embarrassed by the ongoing controversy.
The minister claimed he had met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to express his desire to resign from the ministerial position.
Despite leaving the government, Ishraque affirmed that his anti-drug campaigns will continue, along with his work for the people of his Dhaka-6 constituency.
caption:
A state minister resigns after photos of him displaying a gun during a drug raid went viral.

Ishraque Hossain, the State Minister for Liberation War and Affairs, has resigned from his post. He formally announced the decision during a press conference at the National Press Club on Monday afternoon.

The resignation follows a controversy surrounding an anti-drug operation in the Gendaria area of the capital, where Ishraque was seen displaying his weapon in photos and videos.

Ishraque stated that he held the weapon for his own security during the operation, but claimed that the images were used by media and social media to overshadow the actual anti-drug efforts.

He explained that he stepped down to ensure that neither the Prime Minister nor his party would be embarrassed by the ongoing controversy.

The minister claimed he had met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to express his desire to resign from the ministerial position.

Despite leaving the government, Ishraque affirmed that his anti-drug campaigns will continue, along with his work for the people of his Dhaka-6 constituency.

topic: time bomb found at lalon shrine
headline_marked: Police [[recover time bomb]] near Lalon Shah’s shrine in Kushtia
headline: Police recover time bomb near Lalon Shah’s shrine in Kushtia
summary: The device, containing a timer and petrol bottles, was found near the entrance to the shrine in Kumarkhali.
details: Police recovered a time bomb near the entrance to Fakir Lalon Shah’s shrine in Kumarkhali, Kushtia, around 1am on Monday.
The device was found near a coconut tree to the right of the entrance after officers received reports of a suspicious bag.
The CTTC bomb disposal team from the Dhaka Metropolitan Police recovered two small bottles of petrol, two metal canisters, and a device connected to electrical wires, a timer, and a battery.
An officer stated that explosive material was placed inside aluminium canisters from novelty smoke bombs, while the petrol was intended to fuel a larger fire after an explosion.
The CTTC officer noted that the technology used in the device is similar to a bomb found under a Dhaka metro station in July, although the Kushtia device used aluminium instead of a GI pipe.
While the device may have been made by inexperienced hands, police warned that the spread of this technology poses a serious risk to public safety.
Police have not yet identified who left the device at the shrine.
The July 26 bomb found at Shapla Chattar Metro Station in Motijheel was attributed to the banned militant group Neo-JMB, including 'Bomaru Mamun' and his followers.
